title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the initial statistical preference (individual bias via token logits) and multi-agent consensus convergence (collective bias) in a coordination task (Naming Game) using gendered word pairs such as {man, woman}, {he, she}, {her, his}, and {husband, wife}.
Measuring the initial statistical preference and tracking multi-agent consensus convergence in a coordination game using the word pair {straight, gay}.
Measuring the initial statistical preference and tracking multi-agent consensus convergence in a coordination game using the word pairs {Black, White} and {White, African}.
Measuring the initial statistical preference and tracking multi-agent consensus convergence in a coordination game using the word pair {old, young}.
Measuring the initial statistical preference and tracking multi-agent consensus convergence in a coordination game using the word pair {American, Mexican}.
Measuring the initial statistical preference and tracking multi-agent consensus convergence in a coordination game using the word pair {short, tall}.
Measuring inherent word frequency or preference imbalances using non-demographic word pairs like {less, more} to establish baseline coordination biases.
